p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Vigabatrin, an antiseizure drug already in clinical use for infantile spasms in other contexts. Formulation not carried; no dose, route or schedule.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Target population itself (WWOX-DEE with spasms), reports of single children. Genotype varies across reports (predicted-null genotypes in most, a missense in one); CLAIM 001 is a safety claim transferable at T1.
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Already used in WWOX-DEE: CLAIM 001 names eight reporting sources; not a new idea. Its WWOX exposure limit is the finding.
p4_roadmap_fields.known_roads_state: Partial plus exposure-or-toxicity limit; CLAIM 001 status is conflicting evidence and is confirmed as correctly conflicting: efficacy on spasms (n = 2 and n = 1) against MRI toxicity (n = 2).
p4_roadmap_fields.expected_contribution: Symptom (spasm control) to be verified against an exposure limit. Not disease modification (CLAIM 031).
p4_roadmap_fields.mechanism: GABA-transaminase inhibition (the drug's known class action). Context in WOREE: UNKNOWN; the organoid-derived rationale does not predict the clinical outcomes.
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: Internal, WWOX: CLAIM 001, CLAIM 031, CLAIM 002, known-roads note 2.7. Adjacent, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: two cohorts on VABAM and hormonal therapy (CLAIM 001 wave note). The repository's own position for the reference genotype is caution (CLAIM 001, Clinical meaning); this card neither strengthens nor relaxes it.
p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Pro: spasm resolution in one WWOX-null child and clinical control in another, partial response in a third. Contra: ineffective in two others; freedom was clinical not electrographic in one; VABAM in two WWOX-DEE cases; developmental outcome unfavourable despite spasm resolution. Hormonal therapy is associated with symptomatic VABAM in two non-WWOX cohorts; whether it was present in the WWOX VABAM reports is unknown here.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Not assessed in any record read. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN. No latency is recorded in the reports; one report defines response as cessation of at least four weeks, which is a definition, not a time.
p4_roadmap_fields.pharmacology: UNKNOWN for WOREE: exposure, CNS exposure and selectivity not measured in any record read.
p4_roadmap_fields.paediatrics_and_interactions: Paediatric safety is the limit itself (VABAM). Interactions: concurrent hormonal therapy is a candidate confounder or co-factor for the MRI finding in non-WWOX cohorts. Suitability is not presumed.
p4_roadmap_fields.verification_scope: Supported by: single-patient reports; CLAIM 001 itself has had two receipted readings of efficacy papers; the safety anchor has no receipt. Reproduced: no. This card: no audit yet, OWED.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: Was hormonal therapy given concurrently in the WWOX reports of MRI abnormality, and was the MRI repeated after withdrawal? The anchor paper has no receipt in the ledger: reading it is the cheapest closing step.
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Puts the exposure limit and the clinical-versus-electrographic gap on the same card as the efficacy reports, and shows that two 'no effect' reports cannot be signed in the bridge.

evaluation_frame.source: repurposing_10h_scientist-d_20261021.md, 'The answer in one page', DESIGN TABLE A and B. INFERENZA built from precedents that are all NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; the blind audit of that note's manifests is queued and had not returned when this card was written.
a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); the scatter of an untreated interval has never been measured in WOREE
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter
the word protection: nothing in this corpus has been measured as preserving a function that would otherwise have been lost

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.
